title: Principal Software Architect
description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Product Architecture and Safety Teams

Our Product Architecture and Safety teams connect Wayve’s core AI Driver with the vehicle platforms that bring autonomous driving technology to customers. Working across Engineering, Product, Safety, Validation and customer programs, we define how our software integrates with OEM and Tier 1 systems, supporting safe, reliable deployment while maintaining a consistent core product architecture.

🧠 Your day-to-day

As a Principal Software Architect, you’ll lead the technical architecture for integrating Wayve’s autonomous driving technology with automotive OEM vehicle platforms. You’ll work at the boundary between our core AI Driver and external vehicle systems, translating product ambitions and customer needs into clear interfaces, requirements and technical decisions.

Your work will span high-level architecture and implementation details, from sensors and middleware to ECU constraints, timing, diagnostics, safety assumptions, data logging and validation. You’ll bring structure to ambiguous problems, guide architecture work across teams and own key decisions across customer programs. Along the way, you’ll build alignment with engineering, product, safety, validation, program and commercial leaders.

🧩 What you’ll be working on

  • Defining integration architecture: Shape how Wayve software interfaces with OEM and Tier 1 vehicle systems, balancing customer program needs with the evolution and reusability of our core architecture.

  • Making ownership explicit: Turn customer and partner discussions into clear interface contracts, ownership boundaries, assumptions, dependencies and open technical decisions, including what is Wayve-owned, partner-owned, jointly defined or out of scope.

  • Translating needs into requirements: Partner with Product and Engineering to develop actionable technical specifications. Establish a consistent approach to decomposing customer requirements into system and software requirements, including allocation, traceability and change control.

  • Owning architecture decisions: Lead architecture reviews, maintain decision records and make the final technical call within your scope when consensus cannot be reached.

  • Planning for successful delivery: Assess feasibility, integration complexity, technical gaps and risks. Identify dependencies and required partner deliverables to support customer program planning.

  • Building verifiable solutions: Work with Safety and Validation teams to define safety assumptions, integration test requirements and clear evidence that customer requirements have been met.

  • Representing Wayve with partners: Lead technical discussions with OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers, supported by clear interface specifications, integration guides, architecture diagrams and decision records.

  • Leading across teams: Coordinate architects and engineering teams, negotiate competing priorities, resolve or escalate conflicts early, and mentor architects and senior engineers to build a shared architecture culture.

🙌 You should apply if

  • You bring substantial experience in ADAS, autonomous driving, embedded software or vehicle systems, particularly at the software–vehicle interface. Typically, you’ll have 12+ years of relevant experience, including architecture ownership for a complete product or multiple programs.

  • You can define clear product boundaries, ownership models and interface contracts between internal software and external vehicle systems.

  • You understand vehicle electronics and embedded software constraints, including ECU integration, real-time execution, timing, diagnostics and production vehicle software environments.

  • You’re familiar with automotive communication protocols and electrical/electronic architectures, such as CAN, FlexRay, Automotive Ethernet, SOME/IP or AUTOSAR.

  • You’ve worked with automotive OEMs or Tier 1 suppliers and can navigate their requirements, standards and integration constraints.

  • You’ve established and run requirements processes across multiple teams or programs, translating ambiguous needs into clear, traceable and verifiable system and software specifications.

  • You can move confidently between system-level architecture and implementation details, making sound technical decisions under uncertainty and maintaining consistency as programs evolve.

  • You’ve led architecture work across teams and influenced senior stakeholders without direct authority, building support and handling competing priorities constructively.

  • You communicate complex technical ideas clearly through specifications, diagrams and reviews, and enjoy mentoring others.

 

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

 

More about Wayve:

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

 

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

 

🔍 The Interview Process:

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

  • Initial call / recruiter screen

  • Hiring Manager Interview

  • Deep-dive technical interviews

title: Principal Thermal-Mechanical Engineer-Munich, Germany
description:
About Us

We are building Physics AI for hardware design. Our software platform helps hardware designers and physics simulation engineers explore, analyze, and optimize hardware systems, leveraging cutting-edge AI to deliver ultrafast, accurate physics intelligence within the realities of engineering design workflows.

Our first product bridges the gap between the accuracy & determinism of traditional simulation and the speed & scaling of AI, and is redefining how the world’s most advanced semiconductors are designed, verified, built, brought to market and integrated in complex systems.

Role Overview

As a pivotal leader within our European Forward Deployment team, you will drive the adoption of Vinci’s platform among the region's top engineering organizations. In this strategic role, you will build, mentor, and guide a high-performing team of thermal engineers dedicated to engaging prospective customers and demonstrating our software's transformative value.

As trusted technical advisors, you and your team will use deep simulation expertise to help enterprise customers validate and optimize complex, real-world designs. Through these collaborative engagements, you will champion Vinci's value proposition by showing how our platform delivers systemic improvements in thermal performance, product reliability, and time-to-market.

Leveraging strong fundamentals in continuum mechanics, you will guide analyses of complex physical phenomena, including linear, geometric and material nonlinearities, and contact interactions. Your team will evaluate critical factors such as warpage, stress evolution, thermal cycling, and reliability across advanced semiconductor devices, electronics packages, and wafer-scale systems.

You will work closely with customer engineering teams to understand their technical challenges, provide expert guidance, and clearly articulate Vinci’s capabilities in solving real-world problems. You will also serve as a key feedback channel to product and engineering teams, translating customer insights into actionable inputs that shape product direction and drive continuous improvement.

This is a remote role, with close collaboration with Sales, Product, and Engineering in Palo Alto, CA, USA. The role includes moderate travel, primarily within continental Europe. Some infrequent intercontinental travel may be required for discussions and collaboration with the US team.

Responsibilities

  • Build, lead, and scale a high-performing team of thermo-mechanical engineers, setting the technical direction, hiring, mentoring team members, and driving field execution across Europe.

  • Collaborate closely with the sales team to lead technical discussions, scope proof-of-concept (PoC) evaluations, and deliver compelling product demonstrations to prospective enterprise customers.

  • Guide customer engineering teams through the evaluation phase by overseeing simulation setup, running complex test cases, and interpreting results to explicitly prove Vinci’s technical and business value.

  • Own customer enablement through onboarding, deployment pipeline and account expansion, providing senior technical guidance, structured training sessions, and advanced troubleshooting.

  • Provide product guidance and feedback, identify customer pain points and workflow bottlenecks, partnering directly with internal product and engineering teams to transform field feedback into critical new product features.

  • Represent Vinci at major industry conferences and semiconductor events, engaging technically with key prospects and partners through technical presentations and live platform demonstrations.

  • Maintain a strong understanding of competitive technologies, industry trends, and market positioning to communicate Vinci’s differentiators effectively.

Qualifications (Minimum Qualifications)

  • Education: Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related technical field.

  • Technical depth: Expert-level mastery of commercial FEA software (e.g., Ansys Mechanical, Abaqus, or equivalent), with 15+ years of hands-on experience in thermo-mechanical simulations— either as a practitioner running simulations or as a technical account manager for commercial physics simulation software.

  • Industry Domain: Deep familiarity with semiconductor electronics packaging, advanced packaging technologies (e.g., 2.5D/3D IC), or foundry ecosystems.

  • Customer Engagement: Prior experience in dedicated customer-facing roles, with a strong ability to build trust and manage engineering client relationships.

  • Automation & Scripting: Practical programming experience using Python or C++ to automate workflows or parse simulation data.

  • Leadership Impact: Proven track record of prior managerial or technical leadership experience, with the ability to scale, mentor, and drive execution across engineering teams.

  • Communication: Elite interpersonal and communication skills, with a proven ability to distill complex physics and simulation results into clear, high-impact narratives for both deep technical panels and business-oriented executives.

Preferred (Desirable Differentiators)

  • Multiphysics Breadth: Familiarity with thermal management and cooling solutions and/or Electrical Signal Integrity and Power Integrity (SI/PI) workflows.

  • Commercial Track Record: Direct experience commercializing technical software—ideally electronic design automation (EDA) or CAE simulation tools—into major semiconductor and electronics enterprises.

  • Go-To-Market Experience: Prior experience explicitly within technical pre-sales, application engineering (FAE), or strategic technical sales environments.

  • Emerging Tech Adjacency: Ability to rapidly adopt and champion next-generation, physics-based workflows and AI-assisted design or simulation tools.

Why Join Us

  • Not just use AI; be part of a team actively redefining how next-generation silicon and hardware are architected.

  • Work at the absolute convergence of state-of-the-art AI models, fundamental physics, and high-stakes enterprise engineering.

  • Collaborate with world-class engineers and researchers in a fast-moving startup environment.

title: Senior Product Designer - Berlin
description:
About RA

Resident Advisor has been a home for electronic music culture since 2001. Event discovery, ticketing, news and long-form editorial, artist profiles, original films, and a weekly mix series two decades deep. Around 7 million people use the web platform every month, with a wider audience across our apps and other channels. Underneath the platform sits a network of contributors and city managers across dozens of cities, which is how we stay connected to the scenes we cover rather than reporting on them from a distance. RA is 25 years old, independent, B.Corp certified and intent on being indispensable to the artists, promoters and audiences who make this culture.

Resident Advisor helps users explore the world of electronic music, from finding their next night out and buying tickets to discovering the artists, clubs and scenes behind it.

The mandate

We're looking for a senior product designer to join our design team and set the design direction for our consumer products: ra.co and the RA Guide app, used by millions of ticket buyers, readers and electronic music fans annually. The role also encompasses RA PRO, our B2B offering for promoters listing events and tickets on RA.

You'll work closely with Product Managers, Engineers, Data, Commercial and Growth teams to design experiences that help users stay engaged with the electronic music community via RA while contributing to the future development of the platform.

This is a senior role for a designer who combines strong product thinking and exceptional craft with hands-on experience of AI-assisted design. You'll lead projects from discovery through delivery, set the standard for design quality across the team, and own the evolution of the RA Design System so it works as well for AI tools and agents as it does for designers and engineers.

Responsibilities

Product design and leadership

  • Lead design for Resident Advisor's consumer products end to end, across web and native app touchpoints.
  • Set design direction and quality standards, and partner with Product, Engineering and Data leads to shape strategy, roadmaps and prioritisation.
  • Mentor and coach other designers through critique, pairing and feedback, raising the bar for craft across the team.
  • Lead discovery activities including user research, workshops and analysis of customer feedback and data.
  • Work closely with engineers throughout implementation to ensure quality execution and close the gap between design and code.

Design systems and AI

  • Own the RA Design System: maintain, evolve and govern tokens, components and patterns so they stay consistent across Figma and code.
  • Structure and document the design system so developers and AI can use it reliably and efficiently.
  • Bring AI into the design workflow, using it for research synthesis, ideation, prototyping and production, and helping the wider team adopt it thoughtfully.
  • Document design decisions, patterns and best practices in a way both people and AI tools can use.

Who we are looking for

  • A portfolio demonstrating strong product design thinking, visual craft and impact on products shipped at scale.
  • 4+ years of Product Design experience, including time in a senior or lead role setting design direction for a product area.
  • Experience mentoring designers and influencing product and engineering stakeholders.
  • Hands-on experience using AI in your design practice, from ideation and prototyping to working with AI coding tools, and a considered point of view on where it helps and where it doesn't.
  • Deep experience building and maintaining design systems, including design tokens, component libraries and documentation, and keeping Figma and code in sync.
  • An understanding of what makes a design system usable by AI: structured tokens, consistent naming, well-defined component properties and clear usage guidance.
  • Expert UI and interaction design skills with a keen eye for detail.
  • A strong grasp of user-centred design and balancing user and business needs.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, and experience working in Agile product teams.
  • Experience designing AI-powered or personalised product experiences is a plus.

What we offer you

  • Generous annual leave policies aimed at promoting work-life balance.
  • Flexibility in working arrangements, offering hybrid or remote work options based on role requirements and location.
  • Matching pension schemes and/or 401k.
  • Comprehensive staff wellbeing initiatives, featuring regular activities and workplace programmes to support mental and physical health. This includes discounted ClassPass memberships and custom-fitted earplugs.
  • Company-led social events, team lunches, and discounts on RA merch.
  • Paid annual volunteering allowance, encouraging contributions to community projects and charities you care about.
  • Regular company-wide Q&As with senior leadership, along with ongoing virtual educational training sessions for all staff.
  • A transparent internal company culture committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion (see: https://ra.co/about/diversity).
  • Active involvement in community projects within the electronic music community (see: https://ra.co/about/community).

More about RA

We are independent and we intend to stay that way. 25 years in, RA answers to the culture it came from rather than to outside stakeholders. That is what enables us to make decisions on a long-term basis.

Our staff, contributors and international teams are not observers. They are part of the scenes we cover, and that is what we hire for. Craft first, and then a genuine stake in this music rather than just a job in it.

RA has been B Corp certified since 2024, which holds us to standards on social and environmental impact we would want to meet regardless of the badge.

We especially welcome applicants from diverse backgrounds, abilities, ethnicities, experiences, gender identities, and sexual orientations.

Our values

  • Electronic music is art.
  • We celebrate the progressive values that underpin electronic music.
  • We advocate for a more inclusive and equitable electronic music community.
  • We honour the past, present and future of electronic music.
  • We use innovation to empower the community.
  • We choose honesty over gain and purpose over profit.
  • We're always front left.

This role is a permanent position based in Berlin. Please note: This position requires applicants to be based in Berlin and to work from the office three days per week. The annual salary for this role is €50k–€60k. If you have questions about the role, please contact

description:
This is your opportunity to join a small group of obsessed game makers, building an ambitious mobile game focused on collection and social.

As our founding UI & UX Artist you will be the owner of the entire UX structure at a high level, down to the UI art pixels in detail. You will work intimately with engineers, artists, designers from the vision level, down to the hands on implementation. Not settling for industry good, but pioneering new UX paradigms, head turning UI art style and hyper juicy interactions.

We’re looking for someone who is passionate about their craft, making social game experiences, and also a student of behavioral psychology. Someone who plays games seriously, but understands that at least a bit of silliness is needed for success. Someone who thinks about all the edge cases, but knows doing it alone, will always leave blind spots. If you feel you have great ability, a growth mindset, and high ambition, then join us at the start of our journey!

Side quest: Read this new page about making new games at Supercell.

What You'll Be Doing

  • UX flow design for entire game experience

  • Creation and implementation of UI screens, assets and animations

  • Involved in pioneering a modern workflow and optimise assets for performance

  • Discover and manage external partners where needed

What You Have

  • 5+ years of experience shipping UI/UX design for apps/games

  • Portfolio showcasing end-to-end UI/UX work on game projects, with examples of UI and UX flows

  • Proven ability to translate game design requirements into intuitive and visually stunning UI solutions

  • Experience collaborating closely with engineers, game designers and artists

  • Passionate about both UI & UX design

  • Range of 2D Art skills (UI elements, illustrations, animations, etc.)

  • Proficient understanding of Graphic Design and Typography

  • A self-starter approach to use AI: you've found ways to use it in your day-to-day work, you experiment, figure things out and bring the same energy to every new challenge.

Would Be Nice if You Also Have

  • At the forefront with AI tools and actively experimenting

  • Enjoys TCGs

Where You'll Be

This opportunity is based in our London office, and because we value a collaborative work environment and genuine human interactions, it is mostly an office‑based role.

Supercell New Games

This is a dedicated environment for building from zero and shaped around a core belief: the best developers don’t need more direction, they need more freedom and fewer barriers. This is where games get the space they need to become cultural phenomenons.

Players are waiting for your vision and ambition to build the next forever game a.k.a. the best work of your career. We back this up with creative and operational autonomy, and the infrastructure, capital, and experience needed to take a game from an idea to global scale.

This is not for everyone. Building towards a billion-dollar game is going to be hard. But let's not kid ourselves: it should also be fun.

You build the rocket. We bring the launchpad.

Game-changing Financial Model

Supercell is great with stuff around benefits and wellbeing, but most importantly you get to focus on what matters: making games. Skip the Venture Capital pitch decks and looking at runway spreadsheets. In exchange, we're offering a compensation model that makes this opportunity financially life-changing.

About Supercell

Supercell is a games company from Helsinki, Finland, with offices also in San Francisco, Seoul, Shanghai, and London. You might know us as the makers of Hay Day, Clash of Clans, Boom Beach, Clash Royale, and Brawl Stars. Our mission is to create great games that as many people as possible play for years and that are remembered forever.

So, how do we make great games? By putting together the best teams and giving them the freedom and independence to succeed. And by taking risks, failing, sharing learnings, and killing lots of projects.

Relocation? Yes!

No matter where you’re moving from, our dedicated mobility team and partners will support you throughout your move. We’ll ensure the process is as smooth as possible for you and anyone joining you – whether they’re family members of the human or animal kind!

title: Special Projects Associate (GTM)
description:
We're unlocking access to the NHS, because healthcare is not truly free until it's truly accessible 💙

The world’s best healthcare, for free. It's not a new idea, it's called the NHS. But the largest healthcare provider is fundamentally broken. Patient satisfaction is at an all time low, and the biggest reason cited is lack of access. So we’re on a mission to fix it with technology that actually works.

We're building the front door of UK healthcare, creating a future where one billion NHS appointments are transparent and instantly bookable, and patients are guided to the right service first time using AI.

We're developing critical national infrastructure. Today, 26% of GP practices in England use our patient registration software, while one in five GP practices in London use Bookable Search to help new patients find and book appointments seamlessly.

Our latest product, Bookable Navigator, extends this vision by automatically booking appointments for existing patients.

We operate from within a working GP practice in East London 🏥 We're backed by Y Combinator, Innovate UK and the NHS Clinical Entrepreneur Programme, and were previously ranked the 8th fastest-growing startup in the UK and 33rd fastest-growing in Europe 🚀

⛩️ Our Principles

Exciting challenges lie ahead. Guided by our principles, we’ll meet these challenges with a thoughtful and caring approach. These principles drive everything we do at Healthtech-1:

  1. 💙 Care deeply

  2. 🏋️‍♀️ Work hard

  3. 🤝 Be your word

  4. 💬 Trust in radical truth and transparency

  5.  🚀 Do your life's best work

  6. 🥳 Find the fun

Read more about our principles and our "why" in the Healthtech-1 Handbook.

🎯 Goal expectations

As our Special Projects Associate (GTM), you’ll be the right-hand to our Growth Lead.

You’ll own GTM tools, systems and special projects delivery. The immediate need is to uplift reporting (revenue and performance) and CRM hygiene. Future special projects may include (but are not limited to) lead generation, sales enablement, enterprise sales support, AE onboarding, etc.

This is an exciting and varied IC role for an analytical operator who wants exposure to strategy and operations in a fast-growing GTM org. We want someone smart, detail-oriented and humble.

🏆 Objectives in your first 90 days

Objective 1: Uplift our systems

You will pick up and own Attio (our CRM) as a source of truth. This means making sure our customer data is current and usable for AEs. It also means making sure we have an accurate way to report and predict our sales pipeline. You will set up Attio well, then build tooling on top of it using AI (e.g. dashboards and maps).

Objective 2: Give the team and leadership clear visibility

You will uplift the way we report to leadership, and within the growth team. You will build and maintain dashboards tracking revenue growth, cycle targets and product adoption. You will work with our Growth Lead on pipeline analysis. In owning this reporting work, you will have exposure to decision-making on growth strategy and performance management.

Objective 3: Enable the growth team to sell more

The Growth team are your customer and you will find ways to solve their problems and make them more effective! You will build and maintain quality lead lists. You will support AEs with operational queries, targets and tooling. You will build automations and workflow improvements that save them time. You will help new growth hires ramp faster.

⚠️ This role is not for everyone

This is a high-ownership, high-expectation role. You'll be working in a fast-moving commercial environment where accuracy, speed, and proactivity all matter at the same time.

You probably won't enjoy this role if you:

  • Prefer to be told what to do over figuring out what to do

  • Treat ops as a support function rather than a growth lever

  • Aren't comfortable getting your hands dirty with data

  • Are content to maintain the status quo rather than improve it

  • Have never built things with AI

You will enjoy this role if you are detail-oriented, want extreme ownership, and thrive on making people around you more effective!

👍 Required experience

  • You have worked in an early-stage startup before (e.g. in GTM, operations or as founder's associate), where you've owned systems, data or process improvement

✅ Must-have traits

  • Proactive problem solver - you don't wait for someone to flag a problem; you find it and fix it end-to-end.

  • Detail oriented - you’re obsessed with the detail and CRM being the source of truth

  • Love data - you can build dashboards, spot trends, and make data useful for decision-making

  • Bias to action - you ship improvements quickly rather than over-planning

  • Team player - low ego, approachable and feedback-oriented; you get a kick from seeing the impact your work has on unlocking the sales team

  • Clear communicator - you keep stakeholders informed without being chased

  • Great with AI - you know how to leverage AI well, whilst thoroughly checking accuracy

😊 The hiring process (4 stages)

  • 👋 Intro chat - with our Talent Partner, to learn more about each other

  • 🤿 CV & work experience deep dive - with our hiring manager, to understand your career journey

  • 💼 An in-office work trial - work with the growth team on a real problem [half day, fully paid]

  • ⛩️ Principles interview - with a Founder, to understand that our values align

  • 🎉 Offer!

💙 A bit about us

💙 We’re all NHS staff. We’re inside-outsiders. Trusted with one of the biggest datasets in the world.

🏥 Our office is within a GP practice. This is our unfair advantage. Got a question? Pop down the corridor. Want to learn how your work affects real patients? Pop downstairs to reception.

💪🏼 4 days in the office and 1 day WFH (for most roles). We highly prioritise in-person communication and prefer candidates who want to work 4+ days a week in the office. Our anchor days are Mon, Tues, Thurs and Fri. Homemade breakfast and lunch are on the house every day when you're in the office, ensuring you're fuelled for success!

🌀 We work in growth cycles. Every 8 weeks we do the same set of activities. 1 week outside of Business-as-Usual to research, strategise, plan our work. 7 weeks to knuckle down and deliver it.

🤝 We’re highly collaborative. One of the benefits of a high trust team is we often work autonomously, but as a team we’re very collaborative by nature. Two heads are often better than one, and we frequently lean on each other to solve problems together.

🤜🏽 We’re backed by industry leaders. We’re on the DigitalHealth.London Accelerator, backed by the NHS Clinical Entrepreneur Program, winners of the London Business School Healthtech Challenge, Innovate UK, and Y Combinator (S23).

🚀 An opportunity for real upside

💉 Paid volunteer days. We offer an additional 2 paid days off per year where you can give back to your mission of choice.

🎢 Every 8 weeks we take a day off to socialise as a team. In the past we’ve hiked box hill, raved at All Points East and spent one rainy day at Thorpe park. This works out as 6 working days a year.

💫 Tooling; You’ll have your choice of operating systems and any additional tools you need to do your best work (e.g. keyboard, additional monitors, mouse etc). If you’re on our Engineering teams you’ll receive the latest MacBook Pro and our Growth & Ops teams receives a MacBook Air.

🩺 We know health and family come first which is why we have a generous sick leave policy with additional days that can be taken for mental health leave.

🚕 If you choose to work late in the office, you can expense dinner after 7pm and an Uber home after 9pm, or earlier if you feel unsafe travelling in the dark. This is optional and about wellbeing, not performance or expectations.

We care about building a product that is loved and a culture that is rich in perspectives, experiences, and backgrounds.

Our team represents more than ten different cultures. We come together every lunch time for a home cooked meal, rotated among team members!

We want everyone in our team to know that they belong. We are purposeful about this and are proactively building a company that is inclusive of all people; from race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, neurodiversity, disability, colour, and national origin - essentially every type of diversity. We don’t just want people who fit in, we want them to fit together. We're active in continually improving the way we make this happen.

title: Head of Revenue Operations
description:
TLDR; Conduct's first revenue operations hire. You will build RevOps from scratch: the systems, planning and data our whole go-to-market team runs on, and make it AI-native from day one.

Why Conduct

The world's largest companies compete by being different, and most of that difference lives in the software they've built for themselves, which decides everything from how parcels reach your door to how food gets onto supermarket shelves. That software is a real advantage, but it's also the hardest part of the business to change safely, so good ideas often wait months or even years for the systems to catch up.

Every large enterprise has a software company hiding inside it, and Conduct is building the operating system for it. We read a company's code and processes, work out what needs to change, and help the business and its systems move forward together, wherever custom software has become too complex to change safely.

Fortune Global 500 companies like DHL and Daimler Truck already trust us with their most critical systems, and we've just raised a $60M Series A from Index Ventures, ICONIQ and SAP.

We're a talent-dense team of about 70, growing fast across London and New York, with people from Palantir, G-Research, Legora and Sequoia. Extreme ownership, high velocity, low-ego collaboration. What you build here will shape the company and how the world's largest companies operate.

About the role

Our go-to-market team is growing fast in London and New York, and over the next year we'll scale it several times over, with new account executives and regional directors joining across both offices. They sell a technical product to CIOs and IT leaders at some of the world's largest companies, in long deals with many stakeholders, often alongside partners like SAP and the major consultancies. To grow at that pace, everyone needs one clear picture of the business and an operating rhythm they trust.

Today there's no RevOps function, so you'll be starting from a blank page. You'll decide how we plan, measure and run go-to-market, then build it yourself: the CRM and the systems around it, the planning cycle, the forecast and the analytics that tell leadership where to focus.

We're an AI company, so we expect RevOps to be AI-native too. Agents should do the work that headcount does elsewhere, so a small team can have an outsized impact. You'll work closely with our founders, sales leaders, partnerships, marketing and finance.

What you'll do

  • Build the function from scratch. Hire and lead a small founding team, and set one set of definitions, KPIs and data standards across sales, marketing, partnerships and deployment strategy, so the whole company works from a single source of truth.

  • Own the GTM tech stack. Implement and run the CRM and the tools around it, with clean data captured at the source rather than fixed after the fact.

  • Put agents to work. Design and ship AI workflows for account research, enrichment, routing, pipeline hygiene and forecast inputs, and decide where a human stays in the loop and how the output is checked before anyone acts on it.

  • Run the planning cycle. Own territory and coverage design, capacity and headcount planning, quota setting and comp plan design for enterprise land-and-expand deals.

  • Run the revenue rhythm. Lead forecast calls, pipeline reviews and QBRs, build a forecast leadership can rely on, and deliver board-ready reporting with the story behind the numbers.

  • Set commercial guardrails. Work with our deal desk on pricing discipline, approvals and contracting workflows for complex enterprise and partner deals.

  • Decide where we play next. Turn win/loss, conversion and customer data into decisions, size the market by vertical and geography, and build the case and the infrastructure for new markets.

What we're looking for

  • A track record of building or scaling RevOps at a high-growth B2B software company, ideally one selling complex, technical products to enterprises. You've owned territory design, quota and comp plans, forecasting and pipeline management, and hired the team to run it.

  • Deep, hands-on CRM expertise (Salesforce or HubSpot at admin level) and experience designing an integrated GTM stack.

  • AI-native. You've put AI agents or LLM-powered workflows into production for a business team, and can show what broke, what you changed and the impact. Your default is to automate.

  • Strong analytical skills, including SQL and BI tools, with experience sizing markets and turning data into go-to-market decisions.

  • Equally strategic and hands-on. You design the system and also build the models, dashboards and workflows yourself.

  • A clear communicator who earns credibility with sales leaders, founders and the board.

  • Experience with long enterprise sales cycles, the SAP ecosystem or systems integrator co-sell motions is a strong plus.

  • An appetite for being in the office every day, close to the team and the work.

Your seniority does not matter. Ambition, craft and the ability to turn ideas into high-quality work quickly do. We sponsor visas from everywhere. We're convinced diverse teams build better products, and we especially encourage people from groups underrepresented in tech to reach out.

We build the Cyber Risk Posture Management (CRPM) platform that security teams actually love. By integrating security ratings, threat intel, and agentic AI, we empower organisations to stay ahead of an ever evolving attack surface.

 

We aren’t just building another tool; we’re defining a category. We provide the autonomy to ship world-class technology and the resources to do it at a global scale.

title: LNG Commodity Owner
description:
We Are Sparta

Sparta is the AI leader for commodity trading, home to Leonidas AI, the first operating system for oil and commodity traders.

Backed by $42 million in Series B funding led by One Peak, with participation from returning investors FirstMark and Singular, the same investors behind AI leaders like Legora, Dataiku, and Synthesia. Most companies are building a chatbot on top of data. We've built an agent with an actual reasoning layer, grounded in years of proprietary market data and in-house trading expertise nobody else has.

We're scaling fast, and it's an exciting time to join. From independents to multinationals, the world's leading commodity teams use Sparta and Leonidas AI to move faster, trade smarter, and stay ahead of the market.

At Sparta, you'll be trusted to take ownership, backed by a team who wants you to succeed. AI is how we build here, not just what we sell. Good ideas move fast, and yours could go from staging to production in a couple of hours, whatever department you're in. You'll be challenged, supported, and given room to grow, building the AI that's changing how commodity trading gets done.

Your work has reach. From shaping Leonidas AI, to powering smarter decisions for traders around the world, to changing how commodity trading is done. And because we're growing fast, you'll accelerate your career with a level of ownership and impact you simply won't get at bigger, slower-moving companies.

LNG Commodity Owner, Sparta Commodities

Singapore, Geneva or London

 

LNG moves on netbacks, shipping and a handful of hubs that rarely agree with each other. Plenty of people write about that. We want the person who builds the system that connects all the pieces of the puzzle, and then puts it in front of traders and makes it sell.

Sparta is building the data platform that energy traders, analysts and commercial teams use to make faster, better decisions. We cover forward curves, price assessments, market intelligence and trade flows across the global energy complex. LNG is our next vertical, and we want an exceptional builder to lead it.

 

The role

 

This is a builder's seat. It isn't just an analyst position, a sales role or a thought-leadership seat. You will be leading the development of Sparta's LNG offering, from the first netback model to the AI analyst that puts together a forward view on LNG markets autonomously, working with our engineering, product, data and commercial teams. You will set the direction and stay hands-on: prototyping, testing and shipping with the team, not handing over a spec and waiting. Building on its own is not enough. The job is to build a product LNG desks will pay for, which means time with clients is as much a part of the role as time in the code.

 

We are looking for someone who knows LNG deeply: JKM, TTF and Henry Hub relationships, netbacks and delivered economics, shipping and regasification costs, cargo arbitrage between basins and contract structures. Your job is to turn that knowledge into products. Expect a good part of your week to be hands-on with AI coding tools: prototyping a pricing model in Python, standing up a data pipeline, creating market-leading knowledge graphs that an AI agent follows and testing its answers against desk judgement. The rest goes on working with engineers to harden, scale and ship what the team builds.

 

The role reports to our Head of Commodities.

 

What you'll do

 

Building products, data pipelines and AI agents (~55% of role)

  • Lead the design and build of Sparta's LNG product set: netbacks, arbitrage routes, delivered price curves and the analytical tools that sit on top of them

  • Build the LNG expert inside Leonidas with our AI engineers: the tools it calls, the domain rules it follows and the knowledge base behind them

  • Build automated products with the team: a daily LNG brief autonomously written by AI analyst, alerts on the curves and spreads that matter, and the quality checks that catch errors before clients see them

  • Build evaluation sets that test the AI against desk judgement, and keep them passing as the product changes

  • Build the data pipelines behind the vertical with data and engineering colleagues: price inputs, freight and regas assumptions, vessel and terminal data, route onboarding and automated data quality checks

  • Ship to production with engineering through our normal process (pull requests, code review, tests, CI), and hold the bar on scale, security and reliability

 

Owning the LNG vertical (~25% of role)

  • Own the LNG vertical end to end: what we build, how well it works and how it performs commercially

  • Set and sequence the LNG roadmap with product and technology, so clients get something useful early and more every few weeks

  • Write the rules: the LNG conventions, definitions and desk judgement that every Sparta product and agent follows

  • Lead the people working on LNG across product, engineering and data: set priorities, unblock them and raise the bar on quality

  • Be the person the business comes to for any LNG decision

 

Building a product clients pay for (~20% of role)

  • Lead discovery conversations and technical demos with LNG trading desks, analysts and commercial teams, and use what they tell you to decide what to build next

  • Work with sales and account management on the first LNG deals and on adding LNG to existing oil and freight accounts: you bring the market credibility and the product, sales runs the commercial process

  • Give sales a clear account of what the product does and why a desk would pay for it, so they can sell it without you in the room

  • Represent Sparta at industry events, conferences and client visits as the LNG expert

 

What we're looking for

 

Required

  • Deep LNG market expertise: strong working knowledge of global LNG pricing (JKM, TTF, Henry Hub and the relationships between them), netbacks and delivered economics, shipping and regasification costs, cargo arbitrage between basins and contract structures

  • A track record of building, not just specifying: tools, models, pipelines or products you built hands-on and that other people rely on

  • Strong Python and SQL, and comfort with the rest of a modern stack: APIs, databases, cloud services and version control

  • Heavy, daily use of AI coding tools to prototype and ship far faster than a traditional build cycle, and the judgement to spot where an LLM gets the market wrong

  • Ownership and drive: you scope the problem, pull in the right people, get it built and shipped, and fix it when it breaks, without waiting for a detailed spec

  • Credible in front of trading desks: able to run a discovery call and a technical demo, and to hear what a client will pay for and what they won't

  • Experience leading or working closely with engineers, and the technical credibility to set direction with them

  • Experience in a commodity-facing role within energy trading, data/analytics, financial services or a closely related field

  • Ability to turn market complexity into rules, tests and code that make an AI agent answer like a good desk analyst

 

Desirable

  • Experience building AI agents or LLM applications: tool calling, prompt design, retrieval and evaluation

  • Experience shipping work to production alongside an engineering team (code review, testing, CI/CD)

  • Familiarity with LNG data sources: price assessments, vessel tracking and shipping data, terminal and regasification data

  • Experience with pricing, data or analytics platforms in the energy space, or with building one from scratch

  • An existing network within the LNG trading community

 

What success looks like

 

In your first six months, you will have:

  • Led the build and launch of the first version of Sparta's LNG offering: netbacks, arbitrage routes and delivered price curves in clients' hands

  • Built, with the AI team, an LNG expert in Leonidas that answers the way a good desk analyst would, with an evaluation set that proves it

  • Launched at least one automated product, such as a daily brief or a set of alerts, that runs every day

  • Written the LNG rules every Sparta product and agent follows

  • Set up, with data and engineering, pipelines that run and check themselves, so the vertical scales without manual work

  • Put the product in front of LNG desks, helped sales land the first LNG clients, and fed what the market told you back into the roadmap

 

Is this you?

 

This role is for you if you'd rather build the tool than write the note about it, you like being hands-on, you make the people around you build faster too, and you measure what you've built by whether a desk will pay for it. It probably isn't for you if the part of the job you enjoy most is publishing your market view, or you'd rather hand over a spec than help build what's in it.

Why Join Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture is built on innovation, collaboration, and high performance. We thrive in a fast-paced environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are embraced, and impact is rewarded.

• Equity in a high-growth, VC-backed company

• $42M in Series B funding — strong market traction and investment

• Early-stage growth — build your career as we scale

• Market-leading product — we are redefining commodity trading intelligence

• Top-tier tools and technology to support your success

What's the Culture Like at Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture isn't just a set of values on a wall — it's how we work. We embrace a dynamic environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are met head-on, and innovation thrives. You'll collaborate with people who are passionate about our mission and committed to building outstanding products and outcomes for our customers.

The Sparta Code

Understanding is non-negotiable

Understanding leads to believing. Believing leads to winning.

The 'why' is the difference between compliance and conviction. Before we execute, we ask: why does this matter, who does it serve, what changes if we win? People who understand the mission don't need to be managed.

Ask for forgiveness, not for permission

Most decisions are reversible. Most fears are not.

90% of decisions are reversible. Make them, ship, iterate. Perfection is the enemy of efficiency. Bias for action means moving before you have all the answers, but it isn't recklessness. The rule: tell the rest of us what you did, what changed, what you learned.

Fall in love with the problem

The mission wins. Your idea doesn't have to.

Solutions flatter our ego. They feel like progress. But solutions without problems are opinions, and opinions don't move customers, markets, or teammates. The goal is to find what's true, not to win the room. If your idea gets killed because a better one comes along, that's the system working.

It's your fault. Lucky you.

If it's on you, it's in your control.

True ownership sounds harsh until you feel how liberating it is. If every problem is yours, you stop spending energy on who to blame and start spending it on how to fix it. Effective leaders default to 'it's on me'. Not out of guilt, but out of agency.

Conflict is a gift

Honesty is an expression of care.

Withholding feedback is choosing comfort over growth, yours and your colleague's. Staying silent deprives others of the chance to learn. We challenge openly and with positive intent. Done with care, this builds trust. Done with ego, it destroys it.

  • Design and implement new functionality end to end, from initial design and prototypes to fully scoped production implementations, reviewed with the product team

  • Rapidly prototype new capabilities to prove or disprove an idea, then develop a plan for a scalable implementation

  • Pair with designers and other engineers to make the experience intuitive and slick, and integrate third-party services so we can focus our cycles on Tessl's core capabilities

  • Gather requirements from customers and stakeholders, turn ambiguity into agreed plans, and deliver them

Platform & infrastructure

  • Lean into infrastructure work as it arises: our AWS estate (EKS/Kubernetes), infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD with GitHub Actions, and our observability stack (Dash0/OpenTelemetry, Sentry, PostHog)

  • Contribute to the architecture & build of our more complex networking and deployment scenarios, such as private connectivity and multi-region setups

  • Improve developer experience and platform ergonomics so every engineer at Tessl ships faster

  • Partner with our Infosec team so that everything you build is compliant by default, contributing infrastructure controls and evidence towards ISO 27001 and SOC 2

AI-native automation

  • Build or deploy agentic tooling that picks up firing alerts and works through diagnostic steps autonomously, giving a human supervisor a detailed assessment with recommended actions

  • Build agents that keep our estate healthy without human toil: dependency upgrades that test and merge themselves, alerts that arrive pre-diagnosed, runbooks that execute instead of sitting in a wiki

  • Continuously spot repetitive manual work, across product, platform and on-call workflows, and convert it into agent-driven automation

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We're looking for someone who is as excited as we are to be part of a dynamic team that is shaping the future of AI and software development. We're committed to building a diverse team and strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences.

Must-haves

  • Proven experience as a Software Engineer (TypeScript/Node preferred): you care about code modularity, structure and aesthetics, and you're equally comfortable contributing to a mature codebase with strict CI criteria or hacking up a quick prototype to prove an assumption

  • A genuine pull towards platform and infrastructure work, backed by hands-on experience: you've deployed and operated real systems (Kubernetes, cloud environments, infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD), and when the chance came to go deeper, you took it, whether that was owning platform or DevOps work in a previous role or picking up the infrastructure tasks nobody else wanted

  • Solid systems and networking fundamentals: DNS, TLS, VPCs, firewalls; you can reason and debug below the application layer with confidence

  • Demonstrated use of AI coding tools and agents to accelerate your own work, and excitement about experimenting with new AI approaches to transform how engineering is done

  • Comfortable with fast-paced, high-autonomy environments: you turn loose requirements into plans and shipped work without waiting to be told

Nice-to-haves

  • You self-host things for fun: a homelab, your own services, a Kubernetes cluster nobody asked you to run

  • Production AWS/EKS experience, or hands-on work with private connectivity, VPNs, or multi-region architectures

  • Experience producing infrastructure evidence for certifications such as ISO 27001 or SOC 2

  • You've thrived in an early-stage startup before

  • Have a cool project to show us (GitHub links welcome!)

The kind of person you are

  • You're a product engineer first: you measure infrastructure by what it lets the team ship, and you see platform work as making every engineer faster, never a domain to guard

  • You're calm under pressure, including when production is misbehaving and the answer is three layers down the stack

  • You think big about how AI changes the job: the best engineers automate themselves out of the repetitive loop and operate at the scale of a team

  • You're comfortable with ambiguity and rapid change, and you grab a shovel when something needs doing outside your lane

  • You communicate clearly and bring people along: product, security, engineers and customers all need to trust your judgement

Application Process

Here's an outline of what you can expect during our interview process:

  1. Introductory Call with one of our engineering leaders. A relaxed chat to learn about your background, interests, and career goals. We'll also share more about the role, Tessl's vision, and answer any questions you have.

  2. Take-Home Exercise. You'll receive a practical challenge based on real scenarios you might tackle at Tessl: an opportunity to showcase your approach to problem-solving on your own schedule.

  3. On-site Technical Session. You'll pair with two of our lead engineers to build on your take-home exercise. This session simulates working together on real problems and allows us to explore your technical expertise more deeply.

  4. Culture Conversation with our People Lead. A two-way dialogue about our values, team dynamic, and your motivations. Feel free to ask about life at Tessl, growth opportunities, or anything else you're curious about.

  5. Leadership Discussion with Maurilio (Head of Engineering), and potentially also with Guy (CEO) or Dru (Head of Product). Our final stage focuses on strategic alignment and long-term vision. You'll learn more about Tessl's roadmap and how you could contribute to our mission.

Throughout the process, if you have any specific requirements or need adjustments, please let us know: we're happy to accommodate.

Life at Tessl

We want Tessl to be a place where you can do meaningful work, keep learning and enjoy being part of the team. Alongside competitive compensation, we offer benefits designed to support you both inside and outside work.

What we offer

  • Competitive compensation and equity: Market-benchmarked salaries and EMI share options.

  • Time off: 25 days of annual leave, plus UK public holidays, and two paid volunteering days each year.

  • Private healthcare: Vitality medical insurance, including dental, optical and mental health support, with cover included for partners and dependants.

  • Pension: A 5% employer pension matched contribution through Smart Pension.

  • Life assurance: Company-paid life insurance with MetLife providing cover of four times your annual salary.

  • Family Leave: We offer enhanced Maternity, Parental and Adoption Leave from day one to support you and your growing family.

  • Learning and development: We support opportunities to continue developing your skills with a £1,000 per year to spend.

  • Commuting benefits: Financial support for eligible team members commuting from outside Greater London, plus a Cycle to Work scheme.

  • Summer & winter offsites: Twice a year, we bring the whole Tessl team together for a week-long offsite. It's a chance to step away from our usual routines, collaborate on big ideas, build stronger relationships and enjoy shared experiences together. And of course, we have a lot of fun along the way!

Our London HQ

Our office is in the heart of King's Cross, surrounded by London's growing AI and technology community.

We work together in person on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays, giving us time to collaborate, exchange ideas and build relationships. You'll also enjoy catered lunches (Tuesday & Thursday), plenty of office snacks, regular team lunches and socials, plus a pet-friendly workplace.

How we work

Our operating principles shape how we collaborate and make decisions. We move quickly and learn by doing, build on ideas before challenging them, get stuck in wherever we can help, and give people real ownership. We encourage thoughtful debate, curiosity and a willingness to try things that haven't been done before. Read our five operating principles.

We're AI native

AI isn't just what we're building - it's central to how we work every day, across every function. We actively use AI to improve how we work, solve problems and challenge traditional ways of doing things.

You don't need to be an AI expert to thrive at Tessl, but you do need curiosity, an appetite for experimentation and a willingness to embrace new ways of working. We expect everyone to use AI regularly, invest time in learning how to get the most from it and keep experimenting when something doesn't work the first time, rather than defaulting to manual approaches.

We're also big believers in sharing what we learn. We encourage transparency about how we're using AI, what's working, what isn't and how we can help each other improve. Being AI native doesn't mean removing human judgement, it means using AI thoughtfully, while taking ownership of the quality and outcomes of our work.

Everyone is welcome at Tessl

We're committed to building an inclusive environment where people from different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives can thrive.

We particularly welcome applications from people who are underrepresented in technology. If you're excited about the opportunity but don't meet every requirement, we'd still encourage you to apply.

If you need any adjustments or additional support during the recruitment process, please let us know. We're happy to work with you to make the process accessible and comfortable.

Come build with us

We're moving fast, experimenting boldly and figuring things out as we go. There's plenty to build, lots to learn and real opportunities to make your mark.

If you're excited by big ideas, enjoy getting stuck in and want to be part of something from the ground up, we'd love to hear from you!

description:

The Role

Every payment we process runs on infrastructure we built. At Checkout.com, the Cloud Platform team owns the cloud foundations that global payments depend on: a large multi-account AWS estate, a growing Azure platform, and the networking and connectivity that reaches card schemes and banks worldwide. We are genuinely multi-cloud, and we are looking for a Senior Cloud Engineer who is too - a strong generalist who treats infrastructure as a software problem and can deliver from week one.

This is a hands-on senior role in an established, fast-moving team. Everything we run is defined in code, deployed through pipelines, and reviewed like software. You will bring deep cloud expertise across AWS and Azure and pair it with a genuine software engineering mindset: you write Terraform modules others build on, you automate away toil rather than documenting it, and you treat the platform as a product with users, SLOs, and a roadmap.

As a Senior Cloud Engineer, you are responsible for the technical delivery of your team's services. You will work closely with your Engineering Manager to shape direction, manage dependencies across pillars, and ensure our platform meets the standards a regulated payments business demands.

What we are looking for:

Deep AWS expertise: Advanced, hands-on experience designing and operating production infrastructure in AWS at enterprise scale: multi-account architectures (Control Tower, Organizations, SCPs), IAM, KMS, and the core compute, storage, and security services that a large regulated estate runs on. You should have a proven track record of delivering resilient, multi-region architectures.

Azure experience: Real production experience with Azure alongside AWS: landing zones, VNet architectures, Entra ID, and the Azure resource and governance model. You understand where the two clouds differ and can design well for both rather than forcing one cloud's patterns onto the other.

Software engineering mindset: You treat infrastructure as software. Expert-level Terraform: reusable modules, secure state management, and disciplined code review. You are comfortable in a Git-based workflow with CI/CD (we use Spacelift), and you reach for Python or similar to automate what others would handle with a runbook. No ClickOps.

Strong cloud networking: Confident designing and debugging in a complex network estate: VPC and VNet design, hub-and-spoke and Transit Gateway or Cloud WAN architectures, DNS, private connectivity (PrivateLink, Private Link), and enough routing knowledge to own connectivity issues end to end rather than escalate them.

Kubernetes: Solid experience running containerised workloads in production, ideally on EKS/AKS: cluster lifecycle, workload deployment patterns, and the operational realities of keeping Kubernetes healthy at scale.

Security and compliance awareness: Experience operating in regulated environments. You understand why change control, least privilege, and auditability matter, and you design controls in rather than bolting them on. Familiarity with PCI DSS is a strong plus.

Engineering excellence: A focus on observability and measurement: you instrument what you build and answer operational questions with data rather than opinion.

Leadership and mentorship: A natural ability to guide and mentor peers, translate ambiguous problem definitions into actionable technical plans, and raise the bar through your code and your reviews.

Pragmatic problem solver: You understand when to move fast (creating tech debt) and when to move right (paying it off). You are a cornerstone in incident resolution and root-cause analysis.

Experience: 5+ years in cloud engineering roles with significant AWS depth. We need someone who can hit the ground running: comfortable joining a complex, established estate and delivering meaningful work in their first weeks, not their first quarter. A degree in Computer Science or a related field is useful but not required; we care about what you can build.

How you’ll make an impact:

Lead Design & Delivery: Take ownership of large-scale platform projects end to end, from architecture through Terraform to production, ensuring they are scalable, secure, and cost-optimised.

Build the paved road: Design the platform primitives that every product team at Checkout.com builds on, so that the secure path is also the easy path.

Architectural Influence: Work with Engineering Managers and architects to refine requirements and shape the technical direction of the platform, documenting significant decisions as ADRs.

Operational SME: Act as the Subject Matter Expert for numerous team-owned services, providing advanced operational support and ensuring high availability for our global payment systems.

Evangelise Best Practices: Produce exemplary code and documentation that inspires others. You will be responsible for spreading best practices and standards across your group.

Manage Dependencies: Navigate the organisation to manage technical dependencies inside and outside your pillar, optimising for both delivery speed and business outcomes.

Foster Culture: Embody Checkout Operating Principles, using them to shape the group’s culture and acting as an example of efficiency and professional excellence.

AI Integration: Proactively explore and implement AI-driven automation to enhance infrastructure efficiency and team productivity.

Additional Information

Bring all of you to work

You will partner closely with marketing, PMs, engineering, GTM to align design work with go-to-market timing and surface what's shipping before it ships.

This is a team-of-one role with a founding design-ops mentality.   • Partner with marketing, PMs, engineering and GTM to align design work with go-to-market timing and surface what's shipping.

title: RF Systems Engineer
description:
Wanna join the adventure?

Loft Orbital is making space simple. We build and operate reliable, shareable satellites that give customers a faster, simpler path to orbit. By combining flight-proven spacecraft platforms with our own hardware and software, we make it easier to deploy missions in space.

As an RF Systems Engineer, you'll contribute to the design, development, and integration of communication systems across our satellite connectivity and next-generation RF payload programs. You'll work on RF system architecture, signal processing algorithms, and performance analysis, collaborating closely with FPGA, embedded software, systems, and hardware engineers to develop and integrate complex RF technologies.

This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys working at the intersection of RF hardware and signal processing, solving challenging technical problems, and seeing their work go from initial design to in-orbit operation.


About this Role:
  • Contribute to the design and development of RF systems for satellite connectivity and payload applications, including architecture, requirements, and technical trade-offs.
  • Perform RF link budget analysis and evaluate subsystem performance across S-band, X-band, and inter-satellite link (ISL) applications.
  • Develop and optimize signal processing algorithms for RF payloads using MATLAB and related simulation tools.
  • Support RF payload development across the signal chain, from antennas and RF frontends to ADCs and SDR systems, including signal detection and geolocation.
  • Collaborate with FPGA, embedded software, and systems teams to translate RF requirements into implementable solutions and integrate signal processing algorithms.
  • Define and track system requirements, documenting technical decisions, integration activities, and verification results.
  • Support RF testing, hardware integration, troubleshooting, and performance verification through AIT and in-orbit commissioning.
  • Work across engineering and AIT teams to drive successful development and integration of RF systems and payloads.

    • Must Haves:
  • 2+ years of experience in Radio Frequency (RF) systems engineering, subsystem integration, or a closely related field.
  • Proven experience with RF system integration, debugging, testing, and performance analysis.
  • Experience with signal processing algorithms, including the ability to model, analyze, or evaluate RF signal processing approaches.
  • Knowledge of RF communication systems and subsystems, particularly S-band and X-band communications.
  • Experience with RF link budget calculations and RF system-level performance analysis.
  • Hands-on experience with RF hardware, test equipment, and subsystem validation.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently drive technical activities and collaborate across system and software integration efforts.
  • Excellent communication, problem-solving, and teamwork skills.

    • Nice to Haves:
  • Experience with Software-Defined Radio (SDR) architectures and development.
  • Familiarity with FPGA-based signal processing, including experience working with FPGA teams to implement digital signal processing algorithms or IP blocks.
  • Knowledge of key SDR components and technologies, including channelizers, analog-to-digital converters (ADC), and digital-to-analog converters (DAC).
  • Experience using MATLAB for signal processing, modeling, simulation, or algorithm development.
  • Experience translating system-level RF and signal processing requirements into FPGA or embedded software implementation requirements.
  • Experience with antenna systems, RF frontends, and RF payload architecture.
  • Familiarity with RF geolocation, signal detection, spectrum analysis, or SIGINT-related applications.
  • Experience with RF testing, integration, and performance verification in an aerospace or satellite environment.

    • Some of Our Awesome Benefits:
  • Equity, we want you to have an active role in our success
  • Up to 35 days of Paid Time Off (vacations & RTT ) and flexible working hours, we want you to be at your best
  • Health and life insurance, we care about your health
  • Lunch Vouchers, because let’s be honest, we love food! (we even have a slack channel about it #loft-gourmand)
  • Cross-office travel opportunities between San Francisco, Colorado, and Toulouse to learn from our differences
  • Company and team off-sites and many other events to work & celebrate together
  • Relocation assistance to Toulouse when applicable

    Who We Are

    Loft: Space Made Simple. 

    Founded in 2017, Loft provides governments, companies, and research institutions with a fast, reliable, and simple way to deploy missions in orbit.

    We integrate, launch, and operate spacecraft, offering end-to-end missions as a service across Earth observation, IoT connectivity, on-orbit AI, national security missions, and more. Leveraging our existing space infrastructure and an extensive inventory of satellite buses, Loft is reducing years-long integration and launch timelines to months. With more than 30 missions flown, Loft’s flight heritage and proven technologies enable customers to focus on their mission objectives.

    With a growing fleet on track to reach 30 satellites by 2027, we are scaling up quickly across our offices in San Francisco, CA | Golden, CO | and Toulouse, France to meet accelerating demand for space infrastructure.

title: Image Processing Intern: AI-Assisted Tools for CalVal
description:
Wanna join the adventure?

Loft Orbital is looking for an intern to join the End-to-End Validation & Performance (EVP) team and contribute to image-processing and calibration/validation (CAL/VAL) activities for Earth-observation missions. In this internship, you’ll explore how AIT captures and routine onboard imagery can support optical performance testing and radiometric calibration, and turn that work into an evaluated engineering prototype.

Location: Toulouse office, city center (Jeanne d’Arc metro station)
Duration: 6-month, end-of-studies internship — target start date: early 2027.


About this role:
  • Review DSNU, radiometric calibration, and relevant EVP processing and CAL/VAL practices.
  • Work with EVP engineers to identify suitable routine images, metadata, and reference calibration data; document data limitations and provenance.
  • Prepare a reproducible dataset and establish reference baselines, including a holdout evaluation strategy that avoids tuning and testing on the same acquisitions.
  • Implement a baseline estimator: a data-fit term combined with a regularizing prior.
  • Investigate additional AI/ML methods only where suitable training or validation data are available; compare them against the baseline rather than assuming they are superior.
  • Evaluate correction quality, residual fixed-pattern structure, stability across images, runtime, and failure cases.
  • Package the workflow as a prototype script or notebook with plots, quality checks, and an auditable record of inputs, parameters, and outputs.
  • Present findings and recommendations to EVP and CAL/VAL stakeholders; document what evidence would be needed before operational use.
    • The intern will gain experience in:
    • Radiometric calibration and CAL/VAL for space-based optical imaging.
    • Push-broom image characteristics and PRNU/DSNU correction.
    • Applied optimization and, where appropriate, machine learning for image processing.
    • Experimental design, reference-data limitations, and quantitative performance assessment.
    • Building reproducible engineering tools and communicating technical evidence to mission teams.

Must Haves:
  • Student in engineering, applied physics, remote sensing, image processing, data science, or a related field.
  • Fundamentals of signal or image processing and a strong interest in Earth observation.
  • Basic programming skills in Python and comfort working with scientific data.
  • Analytical mindset, rigor, and ability to document assumptions and limitations.
  • Interest in calibration, validation, sensor behavior, or image quality assessment.

Nice to Haves:
  • Exposure to satellite imagery or remote-sensing data.
  • Experience with optimization, statistical estimation, or machine-learning evaluation.
  • Familiarity with image-analysis libraries and scientific Python tools.
  • Understanding of radiometric calibration or data-quality assessment.

What Can We Offer?
You will join a stimulating environment, surrounded by passionate engineers, conducive to learning, innovation, and personal and professional development — and help build the future of space infrastructure. With a growing fleet on track to reach 30 satellites by 2027, we are scaling up quickly across our offices in San Francisco, USA | Golden, USA | and Toulouse, France.

title: AI/ML Engineering Intern: System 1 Models for Reactive Space Operations
description:
Wanna join the adventure?

Loft Orbital flies other people's payloads on standardized satellites, giving our customers a fast, simple, and reliable path to orbit. Our AI for Space team is looking for a motivated intern to explore how fast, lightweight “System 1” models can boost reactivity, performance, and usability across our satellite operational chains.

Reactivity use cases are at the heart of Loft's vision, and we are scaling them: from single-satellite reactive loops, to two-satellite / two-sensor tip & cue (a detection from one sensor automatically cueing an acquisition by another), and ultimately multi-satellite scenarios. Today we mostly rely on “System 2” models — powerful but slow and heavy at inference — from our partners. “System 1” models (fast, intuitive) are coming back strongly and could add value not only on reactivity, but also on performance and ease of use. This internship will assess that added value and prototype it on our reactivity scenarios.

Location: Toulouse office, city center (Jeanne d’Arc metro station)
Duration: 6-month, end-of-studies internship — target start date: early 2027.


About this role:
  • Review the state of the art on System 1 / fast, intuitive models and compare them with the System 2 models used today, including our partners' models.
  • Map where System 1 models could bring value in our operational chain for reactivity use cases, from detection to tasking.
  • Define benchmark scenarios of increasing complexity with the team: a single-satellite reactive loop, then a two-satellite / two-sensor tip & cue loop, and, as a stretch goal, a multi-satellite scenario.
  • Set the latency budget, accuracy needs, and execution context for each scenario.
  • Build datasets and evaluation sets from Loft data, partner outputs, and open datasets.
  • Train or fine-tune System 1 models and benchmark them against System 2 baselines on reactivity (latency), performance (accuracy, compute footprint), and ease of use (integration and operational effort).
  • Prototype an end-to-end reactive loop, possibly as a hybrid design where System 1 triggers and System 2 validates, and assess how it extends to multi-satellite coordination.
  • Document results and recommendations for production use, and deliver a final demo.

Must Haves:
  • Final-year engineering or Master's student specialized in ML / deep learning / computer vision.
  • Solid Python and PyTorch skills, and good software engineering practices.
  • Strong understanding of the state of the art in LLM / VLM / Reinforcement Learning.
  • Practical experience training neural networks (language models or computer vision) and/or LLM manipulation.

Nice to Haves:
  • Model optimization (quantization, distillation, edge inference).

What Can We Offer?
You will join the AI for Space team and directly support the scaling of reactivity use cases, a core part of Loft's vision — working toward shorter detection-to-tasking latency on single-satellite and tip & cue scenarios, and a first step towards multi-satellite reactive operations.
